notes.note: Starting with Firefox 156, Firefox Nightly enables Vulkan hardware video decoding on Linux for recent NVIDIA graphics cards.
Firefox on macOS can now be set to open automatically when the computer starts up, from the Startup section of Settings.
Starting with Firefox 156, tabbing into the search bar in Firefox Nightly lands on the search input rather than the search button

On [Firefox for Android][1], the media notification now shows previous, next, and a timeline for seeking through audio and video.


  [1]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mozilla.fenix
Starting with Firefox 155, the RegExp Buffer Boundary proposal is now available for testing in Nightly builds by setting the `javascript.options.experimental.regexp_buffer_boundaries` preference.

Starting in Firefox 155, the CSS Typed Object Model's `StylePropertyMap` now supports [`delete()`][1] for removing a property in Nightly builds.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/StylePropertyMap/delete

Starting with Firefox 155, Firefox Nightly offers limited support for the [Speculation Rules API][1] for same-origin prefetch, allowing pages to declare which links should be prefetched. This initial support covers only the `immediate` eagerness level and `list` source rules.
[1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Speculation_Rules_API

Starting with Firefox 155, Nightly builds enable the [Audio Session API][1], letting sites declare how their audio mixes with other applications.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/AudioSession

Starting with Firefox 155, Nightly builds now support the [`at-rule()`][1] function for `@supports`. This allows authors to test for browser support of specific at-rules, such as `@supports at-rule(@scope)`.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/At-rules/@supports#at-rule

Starting with Firefox 155, Firefox Nightly supports [typed arithmetic][1] in CSS `calc()`, allowing units to be multiplied and divided within math functions.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Values_and_units/Using_typed_arithmetic
Starting with Firefox 155, Firefox Nightly supports the `<a>` element in the MathML namespace, exposed via the new `MathMLAnchorElement` WebIDL interface, so mathematical expressions can be links.

The [FirefoxHome][1] policy now has a Widgets option, letting administrators control whether the new tab page productivity widgets are available.


  [1]: https://firefox-admin-docs.mozilla.org/reference/policies/firefoxhome/
The `SitePolicies` policy now supports `DisableServiceWorkers`, letting administrators block service worker registration on specific sites.
The Windows installer now resolves /INI= paths relative to the installer itself, so deployment tools that unpack to a temporary folder no longer need an absolute path.
Fixed WebCodecs VideoEncoder hanging on macOS when encoding a VideoFrame in NV12 format.
The centering of content inside buttons and text inputs is now expressed with align-content in the built-in stylesheet, so pages can override it.
On Windows devices with ARM64 processors, WebRTC video calls may now use hardware H264 decoding instead of falling back to software
Fixed dragging an image to a new position in a rich-text editor replacing it with a long line of text instead of moving it.

[text-box-trim][1] now uses the font metrics of a `::first-line` pseudo-element when one applies, matching other browsers and the specification.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/text-box-trim
On all devices, WebRTC video calls may now use hardware AV1 decoding instead of falling back to software

Starting with Firefox 154, Firefox Nightly is testing a simpler tab context menu in Firefox Labs. It can be turned on in *Settings > Firefox Labs > Streamline tab menu*, and feedback is welcome on [Mozilla Connect][1].

  [1]: https://connect.mozilla.org/t5/discussions/try-streamlined-tab-menu-in-nightly-firefox-labs-154/td-p/131285

## Windows

### Operating Systems (32-bit and 64-bit)
 - Windows 10 or later

### Recommended Hardware
-  1 gigahertz (GHz) or faster compatible processor or System on a Chip (SoC)
-  1GB of RAM / 2GB of RAM for the 64-bit version
-  500MB of hard drive space

---

## Mac

### Operating Systems
- macOS 10.15 or later

### Recommended Hardware
- Macintosh computer with an Intel x86 or Apple silicon processor
- 512 MB of RAM
- 200 MB hard drive space

---

## GNU/Linux

### Software Requirements

*Please note that GNU/Linux distributors may provide packages for your distribution which have different requirements.*

- Firefox will not run at all without the following libraries or packages:
    - glibc 2.17 or higher (2.28 or higher on arm64)
    - GTK+ 3.14 or higher
    - libglib 2.42 or higher
    - libstdc++ 4.8.1 or higher (6.0 or higher on arm64)
    - X.Org 1.0 or higher (1.7 or higher is recommended)
- For optimal functionality, we recommend the following libraries or packages:
    - DBus 1.0 or higher
    - NetworkManager 0.7 or higher
    - PulseAudio

Firefox Nightly gets updated every day and as a consequence, the release notes for the Nightly channel are updated continuously to reflect features that have reached sufficient maturity to benefit from community feedback and bug reports. 

**Warning: Features listed here may or may *not* make a final release of Firefox.**

In addition to these release notes, you can follow ongoing development on our [@FirefoxNightly][1] Bluesky account, our [@FirefoxNightly][4] Mastodon account as well as read our [Nightly Blog][2].

You can interact with other Firefox Nightly users and give your feedback to Mozilla staff in the [Nightly Matrix room][3] on chat.mozilla.org.


  [1]: https://bsky.app/profile/firefoxnightly.bsky.social
  [2]: https://blog.nightly.mozilla.org
  [3]: https://chat.mozilla.org/?#/room/#nightly:mozilla.org
  [4]: https://mastodon.social/@FirefoxNightly
